summary: Completed focused desktop and mobile smoke testing for the doctor marketing site. Hero, branding, 3D object marker, appointment submission, navigation anchors, mobile menu, overflow behavior, and reduced-motion usability passed.

issues: Production build emits a 1.28 MB minified JS chunk (363 KB gzip), indicating the 3D stack is not code-split/lazy-loaded despite Suspense; review performance on slower mobile devices.

action_items: Consider dynamic-importing the 3D hero to reduce initial JavaScript payload.
Add a graceful non-WebGL fallback for browsers/devices where Canvas cannot render.
Consider implementing appointment dialog focus trapping and restoring focus to the triggering CTA for keyboard accessibility.
critical_code_review_comments: AppointmentDialog uses a semantic dialog but does not trap keyboard focus or restore focus after closing.
The CSS reduced-motion rule shortens CSS transitions, but Framer Motion and React Three Fiber pointer/float behavior are not explicitly disabled in JavaScript under prefers-reduced-motion.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Tested at the active Vite dev URL http://localhost:5173 because no frontend/.env or public backend URL was present and port 3000 was not listening. First visibility wait was flaky, but DOM-presence based rerun passed all requested flows.
rca of the issue: No functional issue reproduced. The oversized initial bundle is caused by the statically imported React Three Fiber/Drei/Three dependencies; Suspense alone does not split the bundle.
